stories.title: Bastion wins conditional OCC approval for a national trust bank charter
stories.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency gave crypto custody firm Bastion conditional approval for a national trust bank charter. The approval is conditional, so Bastion must still meet further requirements. A final charter would let Bastion operate as a federally chartered trust bank for digital assets.
stories.whyItMatters: A federal trust charter gives crypto custody firms a clearer regulatory path, which matters for institutional adoption of digital assets.
whatToWatch: Whether Bastion meets the OCC's remaining conditions
Timeline for final charter approval
questions: What conditions did the OCC attach to the approval?
How does this compare to other crypto firms' trust charter bids?

sources.title: Bastion wins conditional OCC approval for national trust bank charter

stories.title: Bitcoin faces an October 18 test as Trump prepares new Russia tariffs
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that bitcoin faces a key test around October 18, tied to the Trump administration's plans for new tariffs on Russia. The tariff move could add macro uncertainty that spills over into risk assets, including crypto.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin increasingly trades on macro and geopolitical headlines, so new tariff action could drive short-term volatility.
whatToWatch: The October 18 tariff decision
Bitcoin's price reaction around that date
questions: How strong is the historical link between tariff news and bitcoin price moves?

stories.title: Clarity Act's defeat leaves the SEC and CFTC in charge of crypto rules
stories.summary: The Clarity Act, a bill meant to set clear federal rules for crypto market structure, failed to pass. Decrypt reports that its defeat leaves the SEC and CFTC as the main drivers of crypto policy, through their own rules and enforcement rather than new legislation.
stories.whyItMatters: Without a market-structure law, crypto firms stay subject to case-by-case regulatory decisions, which prolongs legal uncertainty.
whatToWatch: New SEC or CFTC rulemaking and enforcement on crypto
Any renewed push in Congress for a replacement bill
questions: Why did the Clarity Act fail?
Will Congress try again with a new version?

sources.title: How the Clarity Act's Defeat Handed the SEC and CFTC the Wheel on Crypto

stories.title: Brazil blocks stablecoins from a key cross-border payment rail
stories.summary: Brazil has moved to block stablecoins from a major cross-border payment rail, CryptoSlate reports. The restriction comes as the global stablecoin market, now sized around $1.1 trillion, faces new limits in some jurisdictions.
stories.whyItMatters: Brazil is a large market for crypto payments, so cutting stablecoin access to a payment rail could slow adoption and signal a wider regulatory trend.
whatToWatch: Brazilian regulators' next steps on stablecoin rules
Whether other countries adopt similar restrictions
questions: Which payment rail is affected, and how many users does it serve?
What reason did regulators give for the block?

sources.title: Brazil blocks stablecoins from key cross-border payment rail as $1.1 trillion market faces new limits

stories.title: Bitcoin's sharp rally ran mostly on short liquidations, not new buying
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that bitcoin's sharpest rally in two years came mainly from short-position liquidations rather than fresh spot demand. Forced buying by traders closing short bets can push prices up fast without lasting demand behind it.
stories.whyItMatters: A rally built on liquidations rather than organic buying may be less likely to hold, which matters for anyone reading the price move as a demand signal.
whatToWatch: Whether spot buying volume rises to support the higher price
Further liquidation data in coming days
questions: How much of the rally has since reversed?
What triggered the initial short squeeze?

sources.title: Bitcoin's Sharpest Rally in Two Years Ran Almost Entirely on Short Liquidations

stories.title: Zcash's 100% rally pushes Grayscale's ZEC ETF within $85 million of $1 billion
stories.summary: Zcash (ZEC) has rallied about 100% to above $1,500, CryptoSlate reports. The surge has pushed assets in Grayscale's Zcash ETF to within $85 million of $1 billion.
stories.whyItMatters: A privacy coin nearing mainstream ETF scale is notable, given regulators' past wariness toward privacy-focused crypto assets.
whatToWatch: Whether the Grayscale Zcash ETF crosses $1 billion in assets
Whether ZEC's rally holds or reverses
questions: What is driving the sudden demand for ZEC?
How much of the ETF inflow is new money versus price appreciation?

stories.whyItMatters: This level may decide whether bitcoin's recent resilience continues or gives way to a deeper pullback.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin's price action near $82,000 this weekend
Weekend trading volume, which tends to be thinner and more volatile
questions: What makes $82,000 a significant technical level here?

stories.title: VanEck criticizes Metaplanet over executive dilution despite pay cuts
stories.summary: Asset manager VanEck has criticized Japanese bitcoin treasury company Metaplanet, saying executive stock dilution remains a problem even after the company cut compensation, Cointelegraph reports.
stories.whyItMatters: Dilution concerns at bitcoin treasury companies matter to investors who treat these firms as a proxy for bitcoin exposure.
whatToWatch: Metaplanet's response to VanEck's criticism
Any change to Metaplanet's executive pay or share structure
questions: How much dilution has occurred, and from which equity grants?

stories.title: Grayscale cuts fees on its red-hot Zcash ETF
stories.summary: Grayscale is lowering the cost of its Zcash ETF, Decrypt reports, as the fund has drawn strong inflows amid ZEC's recent price surge.
stories.whyItMatters: A lower fee makes the fund more competitive and could pull in more inflows to one of the market's fastest-growing crypto ETFs.

stories.title: AI gives crypto scammers new tools instead of replacing them
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that artificial intelligence has not automated scammers out of business. Instead, it has given them new tools to run more effective and larger-scale scams.
stories.whyItMatters: AI-enhanced fraud raises the risk for crypto users and platforms that already struggle to contain scams and social-engineering attacks.
